newsitem.title: USA: A.M. Best downgrades Physician Corp units.
newsitem.headline: A.M. Best downgrades Physician Corp units.

text.p: A.M. Best Co said Friday it had downgraded seven subsidiaries of Physician Corp of America after the company announced it would post a fourth-quarter charge, putting in jeopardy its plans to merge with another health company.
The rating agency said it downgraded from B++ to B four health maintenance organizations and three life insurance subsidiaries.

Earlier Friday, Physician said it expected to take a charge of about $80 million in its fourth quarter due to increased liabilities associated with its workers compensation division. It had already taken a $130 million charge for the same division in November.
Sierra Health Services Inc later said it saw the charge as an "adverse development" for the proposed merger of the two companies.
The rating agency also expressed concern.

"A.M. Best believes this development could jeopardize the merger," it said. "This, therefore, raises concerns about the future financial position and viability of the PCA (Physician Corp) organization, given the debt servicing requirements for bank borrowings entered into for several previously completed acquisitions."

The downgraded health units include PCA Health Plans of Florida Inc, PCA Family Medical Health Plans Inc, PCA Health Plans of Texas Inc, and PCA Health Plans of Puerto Rico Inc. The life insurance units are PCA Life Insurance Co (Florida), PCA Life Insurance Co of Texas, and PCA Life Insurance Group of Puerto Rico.
